title: Solo dev, two weeks after launch data: shipping Discord feedback several times a day with ChatGPT for art and Claude for code
author: Mojo2013
selftext:
Hey all,  
  
I’m a solo dev. My game, Guild of Souls, launched on Steam about two weeks ago. It’s like classic WoW, except you play the whole guild at the same time. One hero per class, the rest of your party follows you into dungeons and raids, and you can swap who you’re controlling mid battle.

**Marketing efforts / How people find it:** I make World of Warcraft Forever guide videos on YouTube and point that audience at the Steam page. People who miss that era of MMO are exactly who the game is for, so that has worked far better than cold promotion like emailing influencers / other youtubers / reddit posts. I also targeted dual boxers / multiboxers since that's the kind of player I am after

**How I’ve built the community:** Discord, and speed. Someone reports a bug or asks for a feature, and it’s usually in a build the same day. Most days since launch have had more than one update. Players notice when their suggestion shows up in the patch notes hours later, and they stick around and bring more. It's a positive feedback loop, but getting those first few interested player is a monumental task. This is my 3rd year of experimental game dev, and this is my first game to get this sort of interest.

**Today was the big one:** update 1.2 raises the level cap to 25 and adds a new zone, a capital city, and four new dungeons and raids, plus a pile of Discord requests

**The AI workflow:**

* **ChatGPT** for art and models: icons, creatures, buildings.
* **Claude** for code: features, fixes, automated checks, builds and patch notes.
* **Fable 5.2** for the new models / features / systems in the 1.2 update
* **Me** for direction, playtesting, and saying “no, that looks wrong, do it again” a lot.
* **Discord** for issues I have become developer blind to

Each new generation of AI improves on the last, this game originally started 6 months ago with Cursor but I dropped it as it wasn't good enough. Astra woke this project up, then Claude Code synergized well. Fable 5.2 allowed me to optimise the game to allow much bigger zones / dungeons  / and a capital city

**What I’ve learned:**

* AI makes the turnaround fast. The community is what tells you what to build.
* Passing tests means nothing until you walk around in the game yourself. My own playtests found things no check did. A fresh set of eyes from new players is the most valuable information you can get
* Short, frequent patch notes do more for goodwill than one big polished post.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
